{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"At the foot of the hill, the trail ended beside the old railway bridge. Mara knew it: she and Elsie had crossed it a hundred times, though never with their mother between them and never with a stranger carrying a blue cup.

The girl stopped at the first plank. “I used to count these,” she said. “There are twenty-three.”

“There are twenty-four,” Elsie replied. “One’s hidden under the moss.”

The girl smiled, and their mother made a sound that was almost a laugh. It caught in her throat.

On the other side, town waited in its usual shapes: the bakery, the clock tower, the crooked row of houses. But every window was dark except one, high up in the house at the end of their street. A small golden light shone there.

Mara felt the thread stir beneath her shoes. It ran across the bridge, through the town, and straight to that bright window.

“That’s our house,” she said.

Their mother looked at the girl. “You don’t have to come inside.”

“I know.” The girl turned the cup in her hands. “But I’d like to see the kitchen.”

They crossed together. At the far end, the girl paused and glanced back. The trees stood quiet on the hill, their branches tangled against the deepening sky.

Then the blue cup gave a soft chime.

In its bottom, where the silver leaf had rested, lay a tiny orange seed.

The girl held it out to Mara. “Plant this somewhere warm.”

Mara closed her fingers around it. For the first time, the golden thread went still."}
